title: Intervention Timing
html: We read with great interest the October JADA article by Buzato and colleagues titled “Oral Assessment of Patients with X-Linked Hypophosphatemic Rickets” (Buzato J, De Castro Santos VL, Botelho Pires de Campos MC, et al. JADA. 2026;156[10]:1127-1134.), which provides valuable clinical documentation of the oral phenotype associated with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH). Their finding that 70.6% of participants reported spontaneous dental abscesses, often in the absence of caries or trauma, is particularly striking and deserves close attention in daily dental practice.
